title.en: Life's sorrows and the flowery band

heading.en: What keeps us going on bad days?

hook.en: Everyone has gloomy days, disappointments and people who let them down. Keats asks what ties us to life in spite of all this, and his answer is beauty.

objectives.en: List the sorrows of life that Keats mentions
Explain the image of the flowery band
Understand how beauty lifts the pall of sadness

narration.en: Everyone has gloomy days, disappointments and people who let them down. Keats asks what ties us to life in spite of all this, and his answer is beauty.

body.en: Keats admits that life has much suffering: despair and low spirits, a lack of noble people, gloomy days, and unhealthy, dark paths that we are forced to take. These troubles cast a pall, a dark covering like a funeral cloth, over our spirits.

points.en: A shortage of noble, good people
Gloomy days and dark, unhealthy ways
A pall of sadness over our spirits

narration.en: Keats admits that life has much suffering: despair and low spirits, a lack of noble people, gloomy days, and unhealthy, dark paths that we are forced to take. These troubles cast a pall, a dark covering like a funeral cloth, over our spirits.
Let us set life's sorrows against beauty's remedy.

say.en: On the left, sorrow; on the right, beauty.
Despair pulls us down, but beauty is a flowery band that ties us to life.
Even when good people are scarce, some shape of beauty appears.
Gloomy days cast a pall; beauty removes it.
Through dark paths, beauty gives hope to go on.

body.en: Every day, Keats says, we weave a wreath of flowers, a flowery band, that binds us to the earth. This is a metaphor: our love of beautiful things keeps us attached to life in spite of suffering. Some shape of beauty always removes the pall from our dark spirits.

points.en: Flowery band: metaphor for love of beauty
It ties us to the earth and to life
Beauty lifts the pall from our spirits

narration.en: Every day, Keats says, we weave a wreath of flowers, a flowery band, that binds us to the earth. This is a metaphor: our love of beautiful things keeps us attached to life in spite of suffering. Some shape of beauty always removes the pall from our dark spirits.

problem.en: What is the "flowery band" and what does it do?

steps.en: Identify it as a metaphor for beautiful things and our love of them.
Explain: it binds us to the earth and to life.
Add: it helps us bear sorrow and despair.

answer.en: The flowery band is a metaphor for the beautiful things around us and our love of them. It binds us to the earth, so that in spite of despair, gloom and suffering, we still feel attached to life and keep going.

These sorrows cast a pall over our spirits.
The flowery band ties us to the earth.
Beauty removes the pall and gives hope.
